events.note: Faint CME first seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2024-10-01T01:09Z. Also seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 for a few frames. The source of this CME is likely an M7.6 flare from AR 3842 (S18E30) that peaked at 2024-09-30T23:59Z. The flare and associated EUV wave are best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2024-09-30T23:47Z and are followed by some dimming across the SE quadrant of the Earth-facing disk and some post eruptive arcades.

CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-01T01:25Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely some ejecta  from AR 3834 (~S15W65) best seen in SDO AIA 193 that starts at 2024-10-01T00:37Z.

Narrow, fairly slow CME seen only in SOHO LASCO imagery to the northwest along the northwest streamer, not seen in STEREO A due to a data gap as well as poor image quality/graininess. Likely associated with moving field lines seen in SDO AIA 171 beyond the northwest limb around 2024-10-01T15:00Z that indicate this CME is far-sided.

CME seen to the south-southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and not seen in STEREO A due to low quality imagery; the source appears to be associated with Active Region 3835 (S21W55) despite an ongoing flare and possibly minor eruption from the eastern portion of the disk near the same time; there is opening field lines off the southwest limb as seen in SDO AIA 171 that this CME could potentially be associated with.

Developing CME with bulk seen predominantly to the southeast in early frames with a very faint, oval-shaped/asymmetric halo shock portion, associated with an X7.1-class flare and associated eruption from AR3842 (S17E18). Coronal signatures include an EUV wave and large-scale dimming in SDO AIA 171/193 with magnetic field line movement off the southern and southeast limbs and dimming of footpoints bridging the Active Region 3842 (S17E18) in GOES SUVI 284.

This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A imagery. The source is likely an eruption and rising loops visible starting around 2024-10-02T04:30Z from Active Region 13842 (S15E16) as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. Additionally, there is an M3.6 flare from Active Region 13842 starting around 2024-10-02T05:30Z which is also likely related to this event.

This CME is visible to the S/SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and in a few frames of STEREO A imagery. The source is an eruption and subsequent M3.2 flare from AR 3842 (S18E09) starting around 2024-10-02T13:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery from 2024-10-02T14:08Z to 2024-10-02T17:08Z, in addition to being in campaign mode for the Parker Solar Probe perihelion pass which affects COR2A image quality and cadence.
CME visible to the N/NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Source is opening field lines seen at a high northern latitude and beyond the N/NW limb in SDO AIA 171 starting at 2024-10-02T16:17Z.

CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-03T08:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption centered at approx. N25E70 with liftoff beginning at approx. 2024-10-03T07:30Z as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening can be seen clearly in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284. This filament erupted gradually, so there is a small amount of material seen preceding the main bulk of the CME from which the measurement was based.

CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2020-10-03T09:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption beginning at approx. 2024-10-03T09:19Z centered at approx. S30W15 with Southern deflection as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. Field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

Full halo CME observed in SOHO LASCO, and full halo directed slightly more eastward in STEREO COR2A. The source is an X9.0 flare from AR 3842 observed in many wavelengths but mainly SDO AIA 131, starting at 2024-10-03T12:08Z and peaking at T12:18Z. Also observed as an EUV wave and dimming in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284, with surface brightening in SDO AIA 304.

CME seen to the NW within the outflow of the halo CME: 2024-10-03T12:48Z associated with a filament eruption lifting off near N25W52 or so seen best in SDO AIA/GOES SUVI 304. The CME is not seen in STEREO A well, due to poor image quality and a data gap.

Large loop CME seen to the NE in SOHO/STEREO A embedded in outflow of halo CME: 2024-10-03T12:48Z. Associated with a filament eruption/snapping of magnetic field lines and surge seen best in SDO AIA/GOES SUVI 304 and SDO AIA 171 near N30E60; the signature in SDO AIA 171 is particularly clear, as there is widely opening field line movement off the northeast limb.

CME with an auriform presentation in both the outline of its bulk and shock, seen to the west in SOHO. Associated with a strong eruption from AR 13844 near S10W50 following an M6.7-class flare; an EUV wave is seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

Narrow, faint CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-03T22:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this CME is a minor filament eruption beginning at approximately 03/20:30Z centered at N35E50 as seen in SDO AIA 171 and 304, although the CME itself appears to be deflected towards the North. Minor field line opening is also visible in SDO AIA 171 and 193 as a result of this eruption.

Narrow CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-03T23:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. There is no clear source seen on the disk for this eruption, however faint field line movement can be seen along the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 195 beginning at approximately 03/22:30Z.

This CME is faintly visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and to the south in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source appears to be two eruptions in close proximity to each other in the SW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk. A dimming region possibly associated with a faint filament eruption is visible in SDO/AIA 193 starting around 2024-10-04T02:00Z in the SW near ARs 13842, 13839, and 13844 followed by moving/opening field lines visible in SDO/AIA 171 starting around 2024-10-04T03:00Z in the SW below ARs 13844, 13843, and 13836. The moving/opening field lines are largely visible heading to the west while the dimming appears to have some southern directionality. A third separate eruption from AR 13842 (an M4.0 flare) is likely associated with an overlapping CME feature. There is some uncertainty with this analysis due to the multiple eruptions in close proximity and timing to when the CME is first visible in coronagraph imagery. Both SOHO and STEREO A coronagraphs have data gaps during this event.

A southern CME with a somewhat uncertain front seen with some uncertainty overlapping with the earlier 2024-10-04T04:13Z CME and discernible mostly in difference imagery (not clearly seen in white light images). It is likely associated with the M4.0 flare from Active Region 3842 and the associated narrow, south-directed ejecta seen in AIA/SUVI 304 starting at 2024-10-04T05:00Z.

CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-04T06:24Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The likely source of this CME is a very minor eruption from AR 3838 (N1W52) beginning at approx. 04/05:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 193, although the CME is likely slightly deflected Northward. Minor field line opening is also visible in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

Faint loop CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-04T10:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The likely source of this CME is field line movement seen in the vicinity of S35W30 beginning at approximately 04/09:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-04T13:25Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is an eruption from the vicinity of AR 3844 (S15W37) beginning at approximately 04/12:30Z, although the CME itself appears to exhibit Southern deflection. Field line opening can be seen clearly in SDO AIA 171 along with post eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 131.

A wide CME directly north in STEREO A coronagraph and a bit towards NNE in SOHO. There is a wider shock and a narrower brighter bulk. The shock looks like an asymmetric halo with additional part seen to the west in COR2A. There was no source found on the Earth-facing disk so the CME is likely backsided.
A very diffuse front with many follow up emission. The source may be a broad field line movement over the NW limb beginning as early as 2024-10-04T23Z but the source is unclear.

A very faint front only seen in running difference imagery from SOHO (C2 and C3), but not discernible in the white light SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 imagery (which is sparse and low quality because of the currently STEREO campaign). No definitive source has been found for this CME. This front is followed by multiple similar faint fronts.
A very faint and narrow outflow to the south and southwest.  The source has not been found - but there is a lot of activity in the SW quadrant which may be obscuring the source.

CME seen to the SW in all coronagraphs. The source for this CME is uncertain, with no one distinct eruptive source and the entire southwest quadrant of SDO AIA 171 imagery observing broad field line movement from as early as 4Z this morning, likely due to the numerous active regions in the SW and SW limb.

CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and in STEREO COR2A white light imagery. The source is a thin jet-like filament eruption from on or just beyond the SW limb, best observed erupting at 2024-10-05T11:52Z in GOES SUVI 304.
A very faint front - one of multiple faint fronts today - that is mainly seen in difference imagery and has no clear source in EUV imagery.
Bright CME to the northwest. Its source is likely the inconspicuous  opening of field lines in the northwest behind the limb seen in AIA 193/171 after 2024-10-05T19:05Z.

Faint, narrow CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-06T04:48Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME appears to get overtaken by CME: 2024-10-06T06:12Z. There is no clear source seen on the disk for this event, however some very minor field line opening can be seen in GOES SUVI 284 at approx. 06/04:00Z.

Faint, fast CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-06T05:48Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is seen overlapping with CME: 2024-10-06T04:48Z and CME: 2024-10-06T06:12Z. There is no clear source seen on the disk as this CME is likely far sided, however minor field line movement can be seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 211.

CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-06T06:12Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. There is no abundantly clear source seen on the disk, however some faint field line opening can be seen near the SW limb in SDO AIA 193 and 211 beginning at approx. -6/05:30Z. This CME is seen overtaking CME: 2024-10-06T04:48Z.
Faint, somewhat asymmetric, CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-06T16:12Z. No clear source has been found for this CME.

A faint narrow outflow towards northwest. No clear source have been found for it, although there is a lot of activity in the western part of the disk today. The CME is not seen in STEREO imagery because of a large data gap.

CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-07T03:48Z. Also seen in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is like some activity from the vicinity of AR 3841. There is some minor brightening and movement along field lines best seen in SDO AIA 171 starting about 1.5 hours prior to the CME appearing in C2.

CME first seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-07T04:36Z. The source of this CME is possibility related to some faint field line movement from beyond the SW limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 starting at 2024-10-07T03:50Z.

Wide, bright CME seen to the southwest in SOHO C2/C3 seemingly composed of two or more overlapping loops with internal structure clearly visible and no cavity. Presence of very faint shock may possibly be seen due south in LASCO C2 running difference imagery and may begin to reveal itself to the north-northeast in late SOHO frames after 22:30Z, though disjoint from the main CME body. Associated with a sympathetic eruption resulting from the long duration X2.1/X1.0-class flares (AR3842) located farther behind the southwestern limb than where the X2.1 takes place (W60) as seen in SDO AIA 171 imagery; the CME appears to originate closer to the southwestern limb. Fast, widely opening field lines are also observed in GOES SUVI 284.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery for a few frames prior to a data gap starting at 2024-10-08T03:38Z. The source may be related to field line movement visible near the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery around 2024-10-08T00:40Z. Additionally, there are rising loops/possible post-eruptive arcades visible near the western limb around 01:00Z in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193 imagery which may also be related to this event.

This CME is visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery and is visible in STEREO A COR2 for a few frames prior to a data gap beginning at 2024-10-08T03:38Z. The source is likely related to an eruption near S19W72 starting around 2024-10-08T01:54Z seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery, and is only visible in STEREO A COR2 after the leading edge is out of the field of view due to a data gap from 2024-10-08T03:38Z to 09:23Z. The source is a large filament eruption centered near S25W30 which begins to erupt, deflecting southward, around 2024-10-08T05:20Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery at the time of the eruption, and post-eruptive arcades begin to form around 06:30Z in SDO AIA131, 171, and 193 imagery.

CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and a few frames of STEREO A COR2 prior to a data gap starting at 2024-10-08T13:23Z. The source is likely far-sided, and seen as faint opening of field lines visible beyond the eastern limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting around 2024-10-08T11:30Z.

Relatively narrow CME first seen in the East initially by STEREO A COR2, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in later frames. This event gets quickly overtaken by the X1.8-flare-associated halo 2024-10-09T02:12Z CME. The source of this event is possibly a more minor flare sympathetic to the X flare happening at the same time in Active Region 3853 (N20E63) with post-eruptive arcades or more minor opening field lines and slight dimming seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 originating from the vicinity of AR 3852 (S14E53). This more minor flare is not measurable since it coincides with the more intense flare.

Bright, fast and complex-shaped full halo CME associated with the X1.8 class flare from the Active Region 13848 (N13W08). The CME has two lobes or fronts: the more western, slightly earlier one, and the more central on to the northeast. The flare is associated with the significant eruption marked by an EUV wave, a large area of deep dimming and by bright post-eruptive arcades. There also  seems to be a second eruption - the initially slowly developing eruption of a very large filament spanning from N20W15 to N15W55, to the northwest of the Active Region 3848, which starts prior to the X flare (~2024-10-08T22:19Z). This earlier eruption may be responsible for the more western lobe or front of this CME (which could possibly be a separate CME). The X-class flare could be potentially be responsible for the more central, northeastern lobe/front of this complex event.

A clear, more western loop especially well seen in SOHO C2 (starting at 2024-10-09T02:12Z) and overlapping with a more central front associated with the Xclass flare. The start time was set to 02:23Z to distinguish it from the more central CME. The source of this more western front is likely the initially slowly developing eruption of a very large filament spanning from N20W15 to N15W55 to the northwest of Active Region 3848 which started prior to the X flare (~2024-10-08T22:19Z). This earlier eruption may be responsible for the more western lobe/front, while the flare could be responsible for the more central, northeastern front of this complex CME.

CME visible to the W/NW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and a few frames of STEREO A COR2 after a data gap in STEREO A COR2 lasting from 2024-10-09T13:53Z to 2024-10-09T18:53Z. This CME is associated with the X1.4 flare from AR 13842 (S10W85) close to the SW limb. There is a narrow stream of ejecta visible in GOES SUVI 304 sourced from AR 13842 but deflected to the north and off the limb. In GOES SUVI 284, wide and fast opening field lines and departure of plasma from the W limb is visible. Very limited SDO AIA imagery for this event due to a shutter maneuver.

Likely a streamer blowout, this CME is seen to the N/NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. There is no discernable source in UV imagery, so this event is likely on the far side. This CME was affected by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 lasting from 2024-10-10T05:08Z to 2024-10-10T08:53Z.

Halo CME first seen by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2024-10-01-T09:53Z, as well as in the East by SOHO LASCO C2/C3. There is no clear source seen for this event, however spacecraft triangulation (currently a 26 degree separation) reveals that this event likely originated from the far side, so a source eruption would be too far beyond the West limb to be visible.

Fast jet CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-10T18:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is clear opening field lines seen on or just beyond the NW limb (approx. N12W90) beginning at approx. 10/17:00Z in SDO AIA 193. This CME appears to exhibit a strong Northern deflection.

CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-11T12:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen on or just beyond the NW limb (footpoint at approx. S02W90 exhibiting Northern deflection) beginning at approx. 11/12:08Z as seen in SDO AIA, GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304. Opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

Narrow CME first seen in the SW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2024-10-11T13:09Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in later frames. The source of this event is likely an area of opening field lines seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 193 beginning at approx. 11/12:45Z.

This CME is faintly visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement visible beyond the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171 around 2024-10-11T15:30Z.

This CME is visible to the east/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and is visible in STEREO A COR2 prior to a data gap lasting from 2024-10-11T17:48Z to 23:38Z. The source is likely an M2.1 flare and subsequent eruption from Active Region 13852 (S09E23) starting around 2024-10-11T16:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. Additionally, an EUV wave/dimming is visible around the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 imagery.

This CME is visible to the south in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk at the time of this event.

This CME is visible to the south in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk at the time of this event.

This CME is faintly visible to the south in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk at the time of this event.

This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely an eruption and opening of field lines visible beyond the southwest limb starting around 2024-10-12T10:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery

Faint CME seen to the ESE in STEREO COR2A, and very faintly/diffusely to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Given the observed time of this CME no on-disk source was observed in SDO or GOES imagery, with the closest potential source being be a slow dimming from AR 3852/3854 (around S10E08) starting around 2024-10-12T16:54Z in SDO AIA 193. However triangulation between SOHO and STEREO coronagraphs, with lower confidence due to faintness in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, resulted in a source fit around S10E37.

Slow CME that speeds up in later frames. Appears to be a streamer blowout with a very small streamer to the SW of it. There is no clear source for this CME and due to it's directionality directly south in both coronagraphs it may have a wide range of potential longitudes.

Large messy CME to the W/NW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME. There may be a wide shock feature associated with this CME that is faintly visible in white light and difference imagery.
Faint CME to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This CME slightly overlaps the CME at 2024-10-13T01:36Z. There is no clear source for this CME.

Faint CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-13T17:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this event due to a data gap from 13/13:53Z to 13/22:53Z. There is no clear source seen for this CME.

Bright loop CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-14T00:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is an M3.4 class flare from AR 3848 (N17W78) peaking at 2024-10-14T00:17Z. This flare can be seen clearly in SDO AIA 131, along with opening field lines seen in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211, GOES SUVI 284, and STEREO A EUVI 195. A region of dimming is also visible to the North of this flare in SDO AIA 193 and STEREO A EUVI 195, which is indicative of a more Northern deflection.

CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-14T09:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a very long filament eruption beginning at approx. 14/08:00Z centered at approx. S30W70 as seen in SDO AIA, GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304. Opening field lines are visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195 along with post eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 131, 193 and STEREO A EUVI 195.

Faint CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-14T10:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this CME is minor field line movement seen along the NW limb in SDO AIA 193.

Streamer blowout CME to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The exact source is not clear, but may be associated with moving/opening field lines in the NE of SDO/AIA 171 and 193 starting around 2024-10-14T09:30Z. The front of this CME is very diffuse, but a later front that was more defined was used for the analysis of this CME.

CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-14T14:36Z, although this event likely began sooner but was not visible due to the cadence of SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. The source of this CME is an M1.8 class flare from AR 3848 (N17W86) peaking at 14/13:37Z. This flare is seen clearly in SDO AIA 131 along with field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195. Post eruptive arcades are also visible in STEREO A EUVI 195.

CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. It overlaps in the field of view with CME: 2024-10-14T20:36Z. The source can be seen as brightening seen near AR 3848 just beyond the west limb. Field line movement is also seen in GOES SUVI 284.

CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Overlaps in the field of view with CME: 2024-10-14T17:36Z. The source is likely on the west limb, and some possible post-eruption brightening visible at 2024-10-14T21:27Z in SDO/AIA 304 near AR 3848.

Faint CME seen to the S in C2, C3 and to the SW in COR2A. There is no discernable source in UV imagery found. This CME is likely far-sided, based on the lack of source on the Earth-facing disk and when comparing the position of the CME in SOHO LASCO to STEREO A COR2.

CME visible in the SE of SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely the liftoff of filamentary material from a long filament stretching along the S/SE limb, seen in SDO AIA 304 around 2024-10-15T01:24Z. There appears to be recurring partial eruptions from this filament, so there may be additional fronts seen at later times from this same source.

Narrow CME visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2. Not visible in real-time in SOHO LASCO imagery due to a data gap from approximately 2024-10-15T08:30Z-22:15Z. The potential source is some faint field line movement best seen beyond the NW limb in STEREO A EUV 195 at 2024-10-15T10:25Z.

CME first visible in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 at 2024-10-15T22:06Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The start time of this CME is delayed due to data gaps in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 (15/07:48Z to 15/21:26Z) and STEREO A COR2 (15/13:23Z to 15/23:09Z). The source is associated with the M1.7 flare peaking at 2024-10-15T18:18Z from AR 3848 on the NW limb, around N19W90. Opening field lines are visible in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2024-10-15T18:13Z. The eruption is not visible in STEREO A EUVI 195 due to a data gap in real-time from 2024-10-15T13:25Z-22:55Z.

Faint CME first seen in the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-15T23:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of thus CME is a small eruption seen on NW Limb in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2024-10-15T21:37Z.

This CME is faintly visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement visible near or slightly beyond the northwest limb in SDO AIA 193 imagery starting around 2024-10-16T00:00Z.

This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement visible near or slightly beyond the northwest limb in SDO AIA 193 imagery starting around 2024-10-16T03:30Z.

This CME is faintly visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement visible beyond the northwest limb in SDO AIA 193 imagery starting around 2024-10-16T07:00Z.

This CME is visible as a far-sided halo, primarily directed towards the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery and northwest in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely far-sided as an opening of field lines is visible beyond the northeast limb starting around 2024-10-16T22:10Z in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery. The source may originate from former Active Region 13841, which was located around longitude -163 at the time of this event.

Wide loop to the southwest with many consecutive fronts which overlaps with the far-sided halo 2024-10-16T23:12Z CME. The source is likely a faint slow opening field lines seen far beyond the SW limb in GOES SUVI 284 and in EUVI A 195, starting as early as 2024-10-16T22:50Z and lasting until about 2024-10-17T04:50Z. There is a faint opening of field lines and there appears to be a rising loop departing as well.

A moderately narrow CME to the northeast preceding the wider CME: 2024-10-17T08:36Z. Its source could be a part of the erupting filament seen in SDO AIA imagery spanning from N30E10 to N40E50. The movement and gradual liftoff of the filamentary material can be seen in SDO AIA 304/171/193 and GOES SUVI 304/284 starting ~2024-10-17T06:00Z-07:30Z. This eruption is possibly the source of both CME:2024-10-17T07:36Z and CME:2024-10-17T08:36Z.

A loop like CME to the northeast following a narrower 2024-10-17T07:36Z CME. The source could be the filament eruption seen in SDO AIA imagery spanning from about N30E10 to N40E50. Movement and liftoff of the filamentary material can be seen in SDO AIA 304/171/193 and GOES SUVI 304/284 lasting from about 2024-10-17T06:00Z-07:30Z, so this may be the source of both CME:2024-10-17T07:36Z and CME:2024-10-17T08:36Z.

Jet-like, narrow CME seen out to a few solar radii first at 2024-10-17T23:12Z to the east after SOHO and STEREO A data refilled but the start time is earlier than this; possibly associated with a minor eruption near or just beyond the eastern limb as seen in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284 with northward deflection.

Faint CME with a fuzzy front, preceded and followed by outflows and following the slow/faint 2024-10-18T06:12Z CME. The start time of this event can be a bit earlier. The source is possibly a very minor faint eruption with ejecta/movement of field lines seen on/behind the NW limb in AIA 193/171 starting at 2024-10-18T11:30Z.

Faint diffuse CME to the W/SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3 (barely visible), and possibly STEREO A COR2 imagery (unclear if feature seen to the west in STA is outflow or this CME). This CME is likely associated with the M6.5 flare from AR13854 (S03W82) peaking at 2024-10-19T06:56Z best seen in SDO/AIA 131. A filament to the north of the AR begins to erupt around 2024-10-19T06:24Z as seen in SDO/AIA 304 and appears to lift off with the flare and may be associated with this CME as well.

This CME is visible to the E/NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source appears to be an eruption from AR 3863 starting around 2024-10-19T09:00Z in SDO/AIA 304/171/211/94. Moving/opening field lines are visible in the SE of SDO/AIA 171, however it is not clear if these moving/opening field lines are associated with this eruption or another eruption that may be associated with the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2024-10-19T09:48Z to the SE.
Narrow CME to the south. A potential source could be the opening of field lines to the S/SE in SDO/AIA 171 around 2024-10-19T09Z.
Narrow faint CME with a dimpled front. The likely source is a minor movement of field line behind the northwest limb at latitude ~20 seen starting around 2024-10-19T17:40Z in AIA 193/171.

Minor faint CME to the southeast, becoming wider with time, consisting of a faint shock on its sides. The source for this eruption appears to be movement/opening of field lines just behind the SE limb (lat ~-20) seen around 2024-10-19T22:30Z.

Faint jet-like CME seen to the east-northeast predominantly in SOHO C2 imagery, but also in C3 imagery and STEREO A COR2; it appears with much more contrast in running difference imagery as opposed to white light imagery. Likely associated with far-sided eruptive activity as evidenced by triangulation, although a possible very low confidence source could be the post eruptive arcades on the earth facing disk around N27E70.
Bright loop CME seen to the southeast in SOHO and STEREO A imagery, associated with a significant field line movement behind the southeastern limb as seen best in GOES SUVI 284.

Jet CME seen to the northeast in SOHO C2 imagery shortly after the wide and bright 2024-20-21T09:24Z CME seen to the southeast, possibly overlapping. No major source eruptions were found for this CME, but the CME may be associated with a magnetic field line breaking off the eastern limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 observed near 2024-10-21T11:00Z.

New CME embedded in the outflow in the CME: 2024-10-21T09:24Z seen to the southeast associated with a secondary, sympathetic eruption taking place off the southeast limb following the 2024-10-21T08:00Z opening field lines characterized by new opening field lines seen best in GOES SUVI 284 off the southeast limb.

This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The start time was difficult to determine as this event overlaps with preceding CME: 2024-10-21T13:48Z and CME: 2024-10-21T09:24Z. The source is likely far-sided and related to an opening of field lines and eruption visible beyond the southeast limb in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193 and 304 imagery starting around 2024-10-21T14:00Z.

Faint CME visible to the north in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is visible after a data gap in C2. The source is not clear but may possibly be associated with an eruption near N07E00 starting around 2024-10-22T04:44Z. This eruption is best seen in SDO/AIA 131, 304, and 193. There is possibly deflection to the north due to a coronal hole due south of the source eruption location.

Source is one of several instances of narrowly opening field lines and ejecta from either on or just beyond the E limb at latitude N00, but with northern deflection. Instances start as early as 2024-10-22T03:41Z (very diffuse outflow associated with that instance). There is a clearer instance of ejecta seen at 2024-10-22T07:30Z, which may possibly be the source for this CME, though the timing is rather early. It's also possible the source for this particular front is sourced from even further beyond the limb than we can see in UV imagery.

Fan-shaped CME seen to the SE in all coronagraphs. The source appears to lie on or just beyond the SE limb, observed in SDO AIA 171/193/211 as rapidly moving field lines starting around 2024-10-22T17:01Z, and further evidenced on the far-side around E95 by triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A.

CME seen to the W/SW in all coronagraphs, but not until later frames of STEREO COR2A due to a data gap spanning 2024-10-22T13:38Z-T19:38Z. This CME has a wide fan-shaped front extending further to the southward direction in coronagraph imagery, with the brightest bulk and nose more in the ecliptic. The main source is a brightening between ARs 3860/3859 centered around S05W61, observed in SDO AIA 131 alongside field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193 and some surface brightening in SDO AIA 304, beginning around 2024-10-22T17:04Z. A small filament just to the NE, centered around N03W48, erupts simultaneously in SDO AIA 304 with this (starting slowly around 2024-10-22T16:41Z) and may contribute to the front despite the offset in location.

Faint flux rope CME, which is also a streamer blowout, seen to the south in STEREO A COR2 and south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. There are initially two overlapping fronts seen in early C2 and early COR2A coronagraph imagery: a faint flux rope loop and a more narrow hollow loop which at first appears to travel faster, but by the time both fronts reach the edge of the C2 FOV, both fronts appear to travel as one. No clear source is seen on disk in EUV imagery.

This CME is visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is blocked by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. The source of this CME appears to be filament ejecta seen near S17E80 in SDO/AIA 304 starting around 2024-10-23T10:50Z.

CME seen to the north-northeast in SOHO LASCO and northeast in STEREO A COR2 that appears to be associated with a minor eruption with northward deflection occurring near N19E15 south of Active Region 3864 as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284. Flickering magnetic field lines are observed off the northeast limb nearly simultaneously after the on-disk signature seen in SDO AIA 171 which may suggest, with low confidence, a possible simultaneous far-side component. Triangulation of the CME using SOHO/STEREO A coronagraphs suggested with higher confidence that the CME was predominantly associated with the on-disk signatures.

Faint and fast loop seen to the southeast as defined by its brighter leading edge similar in appearance to the 2024-10-23T11:12Z CME; no definitive source for this CME was found, but could be associated with moving field lines off the southeast limb as seen best in GOES SUVI 284.

Narrow, faint CME observed to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 first during a SOHO data gap at which point SOHO later backfilled. Likely associated with diverging field lines seen off the southeast limb beginning around 14:45Z but becoming more apparent by 16:00Z best in GOES SUVI 284.

Partial halo CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is an X3.3 flare starting at 2024-10-24T03:30Z from AR 3869 (approx. S17E68). Brightening and post eruptive arcades are observed in SDO AIA 131/171/193/335, EUV wave seen in SDO AIA 193, and opening field lines are best seen in SDO AIA 171/193. The eruption is also seen from STEREO A EUV 195/304.

Narrow CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The potential source may be activity from AR 3869, as opening field lines can be seen in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2024-10-24T09:00Z. The CME is partially obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3.

CME first seen in the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-24T11:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This event is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. There is no clear source seen for this event, leading to the conclusion that the source is likely beyond the Eastern limb.

CME first seen in the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-24T11:36Z as well as by C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is some very minor field line movement seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 and 211.

CME first seen in the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-24T12:12Z as well as by C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this eruption is some minor field line movement seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 211.

CME first seen in the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery beginning at 2024-10-24T13:48Z. In real-time, there was no SOHO LASCO C2/C3 white light imagery available due to a data outage beginning at 2024-10-24T12:48Z that resolved and backfilled on 2024-10-25. There is also no STEREO A COR2 imagery available due to a data gap from 13:23Z to 23:38Z. The source of this CME is a small area of field line movement along the SE limb (approx. S40E90) as seen in SDO AIA 193.

Narrow jet CME first seen in the East by SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery beginning at 2024-10-24T14:36Z. In real-time, there was no SOHO LASCO C2/C3 white light imagery available due to a data outage beginning at 2024-10-24T12:48Z that resolved and backfilled on 2024-10-25. There is also no STEREO A COR2 imagery available due to a data gap from 13:23Z to 23:38Z. The source of this event is a small eruption along the East limb (approx. S02E85) as seen in SDO AIA 304.

Narrow jet CME first seen in the East by SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery beginning at 2024-10-24T16:12Z. In real-time, there was no SOHO LASCO C2/C3 white light imagery available due to a data outage beginning at 2024-10-24T12:48Z that resolved and backfilled on 2024-10-25. There is also no STEREO A COR2 imagery available due to a data gap from 13:23Z to 23:38Z. The source of this CME is some faint field line movement seen beyond the East limb in SDO AIA 171. This source seems to be obscured by the brightening of an active region which has just rotated onto the disk.

Narrow jet CME first seen in the East by SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery beginning at 2024-10-24T18:48Z. In real-time, there was no SOHO LASCO C2/C3 white light imagery available due to a data outage beginning at 2024-10-24T12:48Z that resolved and backfilled on 2024-10-25. There is also no STEREO A COR2 imagery available due to a data gap from 13:23Z to 23:38Z. The source of this event is a narrow eruption of material seen along the East limb (approx. S11E85) exhibiting Northern deflection in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304.

CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The potential source may be activity from a cluster of ARs in the southeast, including potential eruption activity from AR 3872, as opening field lines are seen around 2024-10-25T02:00Z near the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA.

CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is an M1.1 flare peaking at 2024-10-25T07:33Z from AR 3873 (approx. S10E72) as seen in SDO AIA 131. The eruption is best seen in GOES SUVI 304. The eruption is also visible in STEREO A EUV 195/304. In real-time, SOHO data was unavailable starting around 2024-10-24T12:48Z, but later backfilled.
Narrow CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The potential source can be seen as an ejecta of material near AR 3873, best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2024-10-25T08:37Z.
Narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and faintly visible in STEREO A COR2. The potential source can be seen around N10 near the limb in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2024-10-25T12:17Z.

Narrow CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely an eruption from AR 3873, near S10E70. An eruption can be seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2024-10-25T14:49Z from AR 3873, and there is another eruption preceding it starting at 2024-10-25T12:41Z.

This CME is faintly visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and (slightly brighter in) STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME and only a few frames available in STEREO A COR2 imagery before the nightly data gap in real-time imagery.
Faint jet-like CME to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. No STEREO A COR2 imagery available during this CME due to nightly data gap in real-time imagery. There is no clear source for this CME.

Faint jet-like CME to the S in SOHO LASCO C2, C3. Data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery. Source appears to be small eruption from AR3865 (S22E00) which is heavily deflected south with some southeast directionality.

This CME is visible as a partial halo directed towards the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an eruption which is associated with an M9.5 flare from Active Region 13873 (S14E56) and X1.8 flare from Active Region 13873 (S16E60) starting around 2024-10-26T06:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. A wide opening of field lines is visible over the southeast limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193, with post eruptive arcades visible in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 starting around 07:50Z.
Loop CME seen to the south-southeast in the outflow of the halo CME 2024-10-26T06:48Z. May be associated with a secondary eruption or outflow near S35E60.

Narrow yet bright CME seen best in SOHO C2 nearly due west along the outflow of several more minor CMEs to the southwest. Likely associated with eruptive activity just behind the western limb as evidenced by opening field lines seen in GOES SUVI 284 around 2024-10-26T07:45Z.
Faint CME/outflow in the wake of the earlier significant 2024-10-26T06:48Z CME. Its source is not clear but there is some movement in the filament eruption in the SE preceding this time.

Jet CME seen to the south-southeast in STEREO A COR2. Unclear source. May potentially be associated with eruptive activity from the southeast, including the recently eruptive Active Region 3872 with strong southward deflection. No SOHO imagery is available to corroborate a potential longitude due to comet observing.

This CME is visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. SOHO LASCO C2 imagery is not available for this event due to an on-going comet campaign. The source is best seen in SDO/AIA 171 as fast moving/opening field lines far behind the NE limb.

Bright lightbulb CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-28T08:48Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is currently not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 due to a data gap that began at 2024-10-28T02:30Z. The source of this event is a large filament eruption seen along the NE limb (centered at approx. N20E100) in SDO AIA , GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304. Opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211, and GOES SUVI 284.

Bright CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2024-10-28T14:00Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is observed in SOHO LASCO C3 white light imagery, but running difference image quality at this time does not capture the front. The source of this event is a far sided eruption seen along the SW limb. Wide opening field lines can be seen in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211, GOES SUVI 284, and STEREO A EUVI 195. Post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 211 and STEREO A EUVI 195.
CME visible to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C3. The imagery it is not available in SOHO LASCO C2 due to an ongoing campaign. The source is likely on the far side.

Narrow CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2 due to a campaign. There are two potential on-disk sources for this CME, including dimming seen around S25E10 in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2024-10-29T01:47Z and a region of dimming centered around N05W00 best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2024-10-29T00:37Z. The eruptions are also visible in STEREO A EUV 195.

Narrow CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. Not visible in SOHO LASCO C2 due to an ongoing campaign. The potential source is an eruption best seen in SDO AIA 171 starting at 2024-10-29T05:57Z, not clearly seen from STEREO A EUV imagery.

Narrow CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2 due to a campaign There are two potential on-disk sources for this CME, including dimming seen around S25E10 in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2024-10-29T01:47Z and a region of dimming centered around N05W00 best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2024-10-29T00:37Z. The eruptions are also visible in STEREO A EUV 195.

This event is visible for one frame in STEREO A COR2 imagery to the southwest, prior to a data gap from 2024-10-29T13:23Z to 23:23Z. In SOHO LASCO C3 this event is visible as a partial halo directed towards the southwest, but the CME is only observable for a few frames before it exits the field of view. The source is a large filament eruption spanning about S37W25 to S15W90, likely extending beyond the western limb, which begins to erupt around 2024-10-29T12:40Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. Dimming is visible around the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 around 14:15Z, and post eruptive arcades begin to form around 17:15Z in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery.

This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery prior to a data gap starting at 2024-10-29T20:42Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

UPDATE: This CME has an updated start time of 2024-10-29T21:48Z as seen in backfilled SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery after a data gap lasting from 2024-10-29T13:23Z to 23:23Z. At the time of this event there was a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery from 20:42Z to 23:54Z, which has since backfilled. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

This CME is visible to the south in STEREO A COR2 and in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery after a data gap lasting from 20:42Z to 23:54Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-30T02:00Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely beyond the SW limb as there is no definitive source on the Earth-facing disk.

CME first seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-30T04:12Z. Also seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely an area of broad and slow moving field lines on the SSW limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2024-10-30T02:30Z, but with a more defined rising loop seen at 2024-10-30T03:25Z. There is also a localized area of dimming best seen in SDO AIA 193 in the SW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk starting about 2024-10-30T03:28Z. It is difficult to distinguish the sources of CME: 2024-10-30T04:12Z and the slower moving CME: 2024-10-30T05:00Z that is slightly farther to the S.

CME first seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-30T05:00Z. Also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely an area of broad and slow moving field lines on the SSW limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2024-10-30T02:30Z, but with a more defined rising loop seen at 2024-10-30T03:25Z. There is also a localized area of dimming best seen in SDO AIA 193 in the SW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk starting about 2024-10-30T03:28Z. It is difficult to distinguish the sources of CME: 2024-10-30T05:00Z and the faster moving CME: 2024-10-30T04:12Z that is slightly farther to the SSW.

CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-30T05:12Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely beyond the SW limb as there is no definitive source on the Earth-facing disk. This CME can be seen in white light imagery from SOHO LASCO C3 but is difficult to distinguish in running difference imagery.

CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-30T07:48Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3. The source of this CME is likely beyond the SW limb as there is no definitive source on the Earth-facing disk.

CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-30T09:24Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely beyond the SW limb as there is no definitive source on the Earth-facing disk.

CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2024-10-30T11:48Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely beyond the SW limb as there is no definitive source on the Earth-facing disk.

This CME is visible to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. It is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to a data gap lasting from 2024-10-30T14:24Z to 20:12Z. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to faint field line movement visible beyond the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery starting around 2024-10-30T15:00Z.

This CME is visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery. It is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to a data gap lasting from 2024-10-30T14:24Z to 20:12Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no related source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk at the time of this event.

This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap lasting from 2024-10-30T18:38Z to 23:23Z. The source is likely related to a faint dimming region centered near S05E55 which is visible starting around 2024-10-30T19:40Z in SDO AIA 193 imagery.

This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2024-10-30T18:38Z to 23:23Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no related source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

Extremely faint loop seen to the West in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2. The leading edge becomes diffuse in C3. The source is some faint field line movement seen beyond the W limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery at 2024-10-31T01:05Z. (The W limb in STEREO A currently equates to W117 from Earth's i.e. SDO's point of view.) Data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 from 2024-10-31T04:00Z to 2024-10-31T09:24Z slightly limited imagery for this faint event.

Faint CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is a small eruption with brightening and ejecta seen in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery at 2024-10-31T02:35Z. Located at approximately S15W75 from the point of view of STEREO A, approximately S15W102 from the view of SDO.
Faint CME visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is unclear in available EUV imagery, and it may be backsided.

CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME is possibly associated with a small filament eruption lifting off around 2024-10-31T07:14Z. The filament stretches from S20-S40 and E50-E70 (centered at S30E60). However, the best fit between SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 imagery suggests the source may be further beyond the east limb of the Earth-facing disk.
